name: Small Business Owner and Entrepreneur
description: ⚠⚠⚠ Half of new US businesses are gone in five years and two-thirds in ten — BLS tracks it, and the rate barely moves between cohorts: 79.6% survive year one, 50.2% survive five, 34.7% survive ten. ⚠⚠ Every entrepreneurship page should open with that and almost none does. ⚠ Florida's own answer is a cheap certificate rather than a degree: 86% of the 2,102 credentials in this field are certificates of under a year.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ ENTREPRENEURSHIP IS NOT AN OCCUPATION, AND THAT IS NOT A QUIBBLE. The federal system has no code for it, because it describes an ownership relationship rather than a job. This page is anchored on GENERAL AND OPERATIONS MANAGERS (11-1021) as the closest proxy — 3,712,900 employed, the largest occupation on this site, at a $105,770 median — but that is what running a business looks like as a JOB, not what owning one pays. Owner income is whatever is left, and for a large share of new businesses that is nothing. ⚠⚠ Nothing here is licensed and there is no credential to hold. What IS licensed is the thing you decide to do: a food establishment needs a certified food protection manager on staff, a child care centre needs a director credential, contracting, cosmetology, real estate and dozens of other Florida trades need their own. ⚠⚠⚠ THE OPERATING LICENCE MATTERS INFINITELY MORE THAN THE BUSINESS CREDENTIAL, and people get this backwards — they study entrepreneurship and then discover the regulator. Work out what your specific business is required to hold BEFORE you study anything general. ⚠ The genuinely useful general credentials are cheap and practical: a Florida sales tax registration, an EIN, the right entity, and enough bookkeeping to file. None of them is a degree.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ The number to know before anything else

The Bureau of Labor Statistics tracks every private-sector establishment from its opening. For the cohort that opened in March 2015:

Still operating afterShare surviving
1 year79.6%
⚠⚠ 5 years⚠⚠ 50.2%
⚠⚠⚠ 10 years⚠⚠⚠ 34.7%

⚠⚠⚠ Half are gone in five years. Two-thirds in ten. And BLS notes that survival follows a similar path regardless of birth year — so this is not the residue of one bad decade, it is the ordinary shape of the thing.

⚠ The first year is the steepest single drop, costing about twenty percentage points. After that the decline is gradual and relentless.

⚠⚠ This is not an argument against starting a business. A third of them last a decade, which is a great many businesses, and the ones that last make their owners independent in a way employment does not. It is an argument for going in with the real number rather than the one on the brochure — and for treating the plan that gets you to year five as the plan that matters.

⚠⚠ There is no occupation called “entrepreneur”

The federal occupational system has no code for it, because it describes who owns the business rather than what anyone does all day. The closest proxy is general and operations managers:

General and operations managers (11-1021)
2025 median$105,770
Employed (2024)✅✅ 3,712,900
Annual openings✅ 308,700
Growth 2024–34average (3–4%)
⚠ Entry⚠⚠ 29% high school, 27% bachelor's, 22% some college

⚠⚠ 3.7 million jobs is the largest occupation on this site by a wide margin, with 308,700 openings a year, and only 27% of employers report requiring a bachelor's. Running things is a job you can reach from almost anywhere.

⚠⚠⚠ But read the median honestly: $105,770 is what running a business pays as an EMPLOYEE. Owner income is whatever is left after everyone else is paid, and in a business that does not survive it is negative. The two are not the same number and this page will not pretend they are.

⚠⚠⚠ Florida's answer is a certificate, and it is the right answer

CodeFL public institutionsCredentialsShort certificates
Entrepreneurship (52.0701)281,425⚠ 1,171
Small Business Management (52.0703)20677⚠ 640
⚠⚠⚠ 2,102 credentials, 1,811 of them certificates of under a year — 86%. Just 144 bachelor's and 110 master's in the whole state system.

⚠⚠ That shape is defensible and worth defending. A cheap certificate taken alongside a job, or while a business is actually starting, is a sensible purchase. A four-year entrepreneurship degree is a large opportunity cost for someone whose plan is to start something — and the credential persuades no customer, no landlord and no lender.

⚠ Where it is taught is the same story: Valencia College awards 514 across the two codes, Broward 338, Seminole State 305. These are state colleges, near where people live, at state-college prices.

⚠⚠⚠ The licence that matters is your industry's, not this one's

Nothing on this page is licensed. Almost everything you might start is.

  • A restaurant or food business needs a certified food protection manager on staff — a Florida requirement for licensed establishments.
  • A child care centre needs its director to hold the Florida Director Credential.
  • Contracting, cosmetology, barbering, real estate, insurance, pest control, salons and dozens more each carry their own Florida licence.

⚠⚠⚠ People get this backwards constantly: they study entrepreneurship and then meet the regulator. Find out what your specific business is required to hold before you study anything general — and note that this site has pages for many of those trades with the licence spelled out.

⚠ The prefix cannot agree on its own numbers

PairCarriersOverlap
ENT1000 vs ENT2000 — both Introduction to Entrepreneurship11 and 7⚠ none
SBM2000 vs SBM1000 — both Small Business Management14 and 3⚠ none
ENT3003 vs ENT30045 and 5✅ USF carries both

⚠⚠ The first two pairs are one subject under two numbers with no institution carrying both — a transfer-matching problem rather than a credit one, because all four numbers are lower division. Send the syllabus.

✅ The third pair is different, and the difference is instructive: USF carries both ENT3003 and ENT3004, which is good evidence they are genuinely different courses rather than one subject filed twice. When one institution runs both numbers and distinguishes them, that settles it.

Necessary skills

  • Reading your own books. Cash flow rather than profit is what closes small businesses, and the owner who can see it coming has options.
  • Customer acquisition. The constraint on most new businesses is not the idea, it is finding people who will pay for it, repeatedly.
  • Pricing. Underpricing is the commonest self-inflicted wound and it is invisible until the year end.
  • Regulatory literacy for your own trade — licences, inspections, insurance, employment law.
  • Hiring and firing, which is the part most owners are worst at and the part that scales or sinks the business.
  • Tolerance for personal financial risk, honestly assessed rather than assumed away.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ Plan for year five, not year one. 79.6% make it through the first year; 50.2% through the fifth. The businesses that fail mostly do not fail at the opening, they fail slowly — so the question to answer before starting is what the business looks like in year three, not on day one.

⚠⚠ Take the certificate, not the degree — unless you want the degree for its own sake. 86% of Florida's credentials in this field are short certificates and that is the sensible purchase. If you want a business degree, take general business and add the entrepreneurship certificate.

⚠⚠⚠ Find your industry's licence first. Food, child care, contracting, cosmetology, real estate — the operating requirement outranks anything on this page, and discovering it late is expensive.

⚠ Learn accounting properly. It is carried at 32 Florida institutions against entrepreneurship's 28, it costs the same, and it is the skill that most reliably distinguishes the third of businesses that reach ten years.

And consider working in the industry first. The general and operations manager occupation is 3.7 million jobs with 308,700 openings a year and mostly does not require a degree — so being paid to learn how a business in your field actually runs is available, and it is the cheapest education on this page.

programs.note: The named credential — 30 Florida public institutions across the two codes, 2,102 credentials, ⚠ 1,811 of them certificates of under a year and only 144 bachelor's. Valencia 514, Broward 338, Seminole State 305. ⚠⚠ Cheap, local and stackable, which is the right shape for this subject.

⚠⚠ The degree route if you want one, and the more portable credential. An entrepreneurship bachelor's is rare in Florida (144 a year) and signals less to an employer if the venture does not work out. ⚠ Take the entrepreneurship certificate alongside a business degree rather than instead of it.

⚠⚠⚠ The most useful adjacent subject on this page. Cash flow rather than profit is what closes small businesses, and accounting is carried at 32 Florida institutions — more than entrepreneurship's 28 — at the same price.

⚠⚠ Customer acquisition is the real constraint on most new businesses. MAR2011 Principles of Marketing is carried by 24 Florida institutions, all state colleges — the same places that teach the entrepreneurship certificates, so the two stack cheaply and locally.

⚠ Named for realism about what Floridians actually start: restaurants, bars, lodging and events. ⚠⚠ They are also among the hardest to survive, and a licensed food establishment needs a certified food protection manager on staff before it opens.

⚠ Another regulated small business, and an example of the page's central warning: a child care centre's DIRECTOR must hold the Florida Director Credential. The operating licence matters more than the business credential.

courses.reason: ⚠ Introduction to Entrepreneurship — 11 Florida institutions, the most widely carried course in the prefix. Lower division and available at state colleges across the state.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Florida carries the SAME subject as ENT2000 at 7 other institutions with no overlap at all. Both are lower division so no credit is at risk, but a transfer evaluator will see two different numbers. Send the syllabus.

courses.reason: Introduction to Entrepreneurship — 7 institutions, the same subject under the other number.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Zero overlap with ENT1000's carriers. Whichever your college uses is the right one.

courses.reason: ⚠ Small Business Management — 14 Florida institutions, the most widely carried course in the small business prefix and the most directly practical one on this page.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also numbered SBM1000 at 3 institutions (Indian River State, Miami Dade, Valencia), again with no overlap. Both lower division.

courses.reason: Planning the Entrepreneurial Venture — 5 institutions. The business-plan course, and the one that forces the year-three question the survival data makes unavoidable.
Principles of Entrepreneurship — 5 institutions. The upper-division treatment for students on a business baccalaureate.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ USF carries both this and ENT3003 Principles of Business in Entrepreneurship, which is good evidence they are genuinely different courses rather than one subject filed twice.

courses.reason: Internship in Entrepreneurship — 5 institutions (FAU, FGCU, UF, USF, UWF). ⚠ Named because working inside a small business before starting one is the cheapest education available on this path.
⚠⚠ Introduction to Business — 29 Florida institutions, the widest business course in the state. If you take one course before starting anything, this is the one that is everywhere and cheapest.
Strategic Planning — 13 institutions. The capstone discipline: deciding what the business is for and what it will not do.
Business Ethics — 9 institutions. Named because a small business owner makes the compliance decisions personally, with nobody above them to refuse.
⚠⚠⚠ Financial Accounting — 32 Florida institutions. The single most useful course on this page. Cash flow is what closes small businesses and the owner who reads their own books sees it coming.
Managerial Accounting — 37 institutions, even more widely carried. Costing, pricing and break-even — the arithmetic that decides whether a business is viable before it opens.
⚠ Principles of Marketing — 24 institutions, all state colleges. Customer acquisition is the actual constraint on most new businesses, and this is where it is taught cheaply.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ A 2000-level course; if a baccalaureate follows, check whether your programme wants MAR3023 instead.

courses.reason: Business Law — named because contracts, leases and liability are where a small business owner is most exposed and least advised.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers business law several ways (BUL2241, BUL3130, BUL2131). Check your catalogue.

courses.reason: Principles of Management — 17 institutions. Named because the occupation this page is anchored on is a management one, 3.7 million strong, and hiring is what most owners are worst at.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. Proposals, contracts and loan applications are written documents that get read sceptically.
Computer Applications for Business — the spreadsheet foundation. ⚠ A founder who cannot model a cash-flow forecast is guessing, and the model is the cheapest risk control available.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers business computing several ways (CGS2100, CGS1100, ISM3011).
